topics.label: Economics of climate change and climate policy
topics.summary: Foundational economic framing of climate change as an externality, integrated assessment, discounting, and catastrophic risk, which underpins every policy debate that follows.

claims.title: Climate Change: The Ultimate Challenge for Economics
claims.rationale: Nordhaus's Nobel lecture: the clearest short statement of the integrated-assessment view, the social cost of carbon, and why carbon pricing is the central instrument.

claims.title: The Economics of Climate Change
claims.venue: American Economic Review: Papers and Proceedings
claims.rationale: Condensed Stern Review argument for strong, early action; read against Nordhaus to see how discounting and risk assumptions drive opposite policy conclusions.

claims.title: On Modeling and Interpreting the Economics of Catastrophic Climate Change
claims.rationale: The 'dismal theorem': fat-tailed climate uncertainty can swamp standard cost-benefit analysis, reframing policy as insurance against catastrophe.

claims.title: Climate Change Policy: What Do the Models Tell Us?
claims.rationale: Critical survey of integrated assessment models and their limits; useful for calibrating how much to trust model-based policy numbers.

topics.label: Carbon pricing and policy instrument choice
topics.summary: How taxes, cap-and-trade, standards and innovation policy compare in theory and in ex-post evidence.

claims.title: Instrument Choice in Environmental Policy
claims.venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy
claims.rationale: Standard survey of the criteria (efficiency, distribution, uncertainty, political feasibility) for choosing between carbon taxes, permits and standards.

claims.title: The Environment and Directed Technical Change
claims.rationale: Shows why carbon pricing alone may be insufficient: path dependence in innovation justifies temporary research subsidies alongside a carbon tax.

claims.title: Carbon Taxes and CO2 Emissions: Sweden as a Case Study
claims.rationale: Leading quasi-experimental evidence that a carbon tax cut transport emissions, with elasticities larger than price-based estimates would suggest.

claims.title: Does carbon pricing reduce emissions? A review of ex-post analyses
claims.rationale: Meta-review finding modest measured effects of real-world carbon pricing, a sobering counterpoint to theory and a bridge into the decoupling debate.

topics.label: Green growth and decoupling
topics.summary: Whether and how GDP growth can be separated from emissions and resource use, spanning the green-growth framework and its degrowth critics.

claims.title: Green growth, degrowth, and the commons
claims.rationale: Frames the green growth vs degrowth dispute in welfare-economic terms and argues the real issue is managing the atmospheric commons, not GDP per se.

claims.title: Is Green Growth Possible?
claims.rationale: The most-cited sceptical case: reviews evidence on resource and emissions decoupling and argues absolute decoupling at Paris-compatible rates is unlikely.

claims.title: A systematic review of the evidence on decoupling of GDP, resource use and GHG emissions, part II: synthesizing the insights
claims.rationale: Systematic review of ~800 decoupling studies; the evidence base both sides of the green-growth debate draw on.

claims.title: Drivers of declining CO2 emissions in 18 developed economies
claims.rationale: Empirical decomposition showing which countries achieved absolute decoupling and attributing it to energy policy and fuel switching, not only offshoring.

claims.title: Is green growth happening? An empirical analysis of achieved versus Paris-compliant CO2–GDP decoupling in high-income countries
claims.rationale: Recent test of whether observed decoupling rates in rich countries are anywhere near fair-share Paris pathways; sharpens the debate with numbers.

topics.label: Transport pricing and road externalities
topics.summary: Applying externality pricing to transport: fuel taxes, congestion charging, and the evidence on whether pricing or capacity expansion works.

claims.title: Automobile Externalities and Policies
claims.rationale: Survey quantifying congestion, accident, pollution and carbon externalities of driving and comparing fuel taxes, mileage charges and standards.

claims.title: Does Britain or the United States Have the Right Gasoline Tax?
claims.rationale: Canonical optimal fuel-tax calculation showing most of the justified tax comes from congestion and accidents rather than carbon.

claims.title: The Fundamental Law of Road Congestion: Evidence from US Cities
claims.rationale: Shows road building induces proportional traffic growth, so congestion pricing rather than capacity is the effective lever.

claims.title: The London Congestion Charge
claims.rationale: Accessible evaluation of the first large-city cordon charge: design, traffic effects, revenues and political lessons.

topics.label: Sustainable land use and land-based mitigation
topics.summary: Land as both emissions source and sink: global land-use pressures, deforestation policy evidence, and natural climate solutions.

claims.title: Global Consequences of Land Use
claims.rationale: Foundational overview of how land use trades off food, water, carbon and biodiversity; the framing used by the sustainable land-use literature.

claims.title: Solutions for a cultivated planet
claims.rationale: Lays out the concrete levers (halt expansion, close yield gaps, diet and waste) for feeding the world while cutting land-use emissions.

claims.title: Natural climate solutions
claims.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
claims.rationale: Quantifies the mitigation potential and cost of 20 land-based pathways; the reference for how much land can contribute to climate targets.

claims.title: Cash for carbon: A randomized trial of payments for ecosystem services to reduce deforestation
claims.rationale: RCT evidence that paying landowners reduces deforestation cost-effectively; links the land-use topic back to pricing-based policy instruments.

claims.title: Deforestation slowdown in the Brazilian Amazon: prices or policies?
claims.rationale: Disentangles commodity prices from conservation policy in the Amazon's 2000s deforestation decline, showing policy mattered.
